oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P0 — Elevated inference latency in us-west-2 (hosted). Pager sent to oncall. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/incidents/latency-usw2. Root msg ts: 1851234567

Jamal (oncall): ack — I'm on it. seeing tail latency spikes across the hosted api route. starting live diag now. tagging SRE.

Sasha (sre): on my way in. preliminary CloudWatch graphs show request queue depth up 6x and scheduler errors around 06:12. looks like some autoscaler flapping + a couple nodes OOM'd. grabbing node logs.

Ana (ops): thanks. I'm drafting a short public notice so we can push to the status page asap. Will post a draft below — please edit for tone/accuracy.

Jamal (oncall): quick checklist: 1) scale out pool manually if safe, 2) drain/restart OOM nodes, 3) fallback routing to smaller model variant for latency-sensitive routes. Doing 1 now.

Sasha (sre): manual scale-out started (added 4 instances to hostpool-hosted-gen). Restarting two nodes that showed OOM. If that clears queue we'll be able to move to status update.

Ana (ops): DRAFT public notice (initial update) — please review/edit:

```
What happened: We are investigating elevated request latency affecting the Redwood hosted inference API in the us-west-2 region. Some requests are experiencing higher-than-normal response times or intermittent errors.

Impact: A subset of hosted API customers sending requests to us-west-2 may see increased latency or occasional timeouts. Dedicated and Private deployments are not affected.

What we are doing: Our on-call and SRE teams are actively investigating, scaling capacity, and restarting affected hosts. We will post updates every 30 minutes or as new information becomes available.

ETA: under investigation — next update in ~30 minutes.
```

Maya (CS): please soften the phrasing around errors — customers get worried by "timeouts". Suggest: "may experience increased latency or occasional errors" and call out workaround: "retry with exponential backoff". Also add a line: "Open support tickets will be prioritized."

Lucas (PM): Important: add a bullet that Dedicated capacity customers are unaffected and call out any features that might degrade (streaming responses recommended to retry).

Jamal (oncall): updated draft with edits from Maya and Lucas — new version below. If everyone OK, Ana can publish.

Ana (ops): posting updated notice (ready to publish):

```
What happened: We are investigating elevated request latency affecting Redwood's hosted inference API in the us-west-2 region. Some requests may experience increased latency or occasional errors.

Impact: A subset of hosted API customers routing to us-west-2 may see slower responses. Dedicated and Private deployments are not affected. Open support tickets from impacted customers will be prioritized.

Workarounds: If you are seeing errors, retry requests with exponential backoff. Consider routing to other regions where possible.

What we are doing: Our on-call and SRE teams are scaling capacity, restarting affected hosts, and monitoring request queues. We will post updates every ~30 minutes.

Last updated: 06:22 UTC
```

Sasha (sre): tiny nit — change "scaling capacity" -> "manually scaling capacity while we stabilize autoscaler". Otherwise lgtm.

Ana (ops): done. Ready to publish once Jamal confirms degradation reduced. Who will hit publish? I can push to status.redwood.ai and trigger an email to customers.

Jamal (oncall): queue depth dropping by ~60% after scale + restarts. Latency tail coming down. I'll hold for one more minute then give publish go.

ops-bot: Scheduled status page update by Ana (ops) queued. Preview: https://status-preview.internal/incident/1851234567

Jamal (oncall): publish approved — Ana please go ahead. :thumbsup:

Ana (ops): published initial update to status page and queued customer emails. Links:
- Public: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1851234567
- Internal draft: https://confluence.internal/incidents/1851234567/comm

Maya (CS): thanks — triaging incoming support threads now and passing priority customers to SEs. Will post any customer-facing questions here.

Sasha (sre): monitoring. queues stable and no new OOMs in the last 10m. continuing postmortem data collection.

Jamal (oncall): marking this thread as follow-up required for root cause analysis. I'll update when we have a resolved notice.

(22 minutes later)

Jamal (oncall): UPDATE: incident resolved at 06:44 UTC. Cause: autoscaler regression + memory pressure on two hosts causing transient OOMs under burst traffic. Mitigation: manual scale and node recoveries, autoscaler patch rolled out to prevent similar flapping.

Ana (ops): Posted resolved notice to status page and sent follow-up email to subscribers. Resolved notice content:
```
Incident resolved: The hosted inference latency issue in us-west-2 has been resolved. Root cause: autoscaler regression combined with memory pressure on two hosts causing transient OOMs. Mitigation steps taken: manual scale-out, host restarts, and a patch to the autoscaler to prevent flapping.

Impact: Some hosted customers in us-west-2 may have experienced elevated latency or intermittent errors during the incident window. Dedicated/Private customers were not affected.

If you continue to see issues, please open a support ticket.
```

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT RESOLVED — 1851234567. Notifying subscribers and closing pager.

Sasha (sre): filing postmortem ticket and assigning action items: autoscaler unit tests, better OOM alerting, and a runbook update to include manual scale thresholds.

Maya (CS): will follow up with impacted customers and summarize any asks from them.

Jamal (oncall): thanks team. Good coordination — will drop the RCA draft in #postmortems in the next 24h.
